As everybody knows, the Summer Sale will be sometime in the next few weeks, rumored to start in just a few days. Does anyone have tips on how to avoid spending too much?

My suggestion is to decide how much you will spend, and put that money into your steam wallet beforehand. If you have a set amount of money to spend that you see every time you log on, it can help dissuade you from too many impulse buys

My suggestion is to make a list of games you really want and buy them when they are a daily deal, flash sale, the community's choice or it's the last day of sale. Don't buy games that are not on your list just because they're cheap. You're probably never going to play them.

Be sure to also check out sales on other pages like GMG or GOG. They often have better discounts then steam.

Excuse the PCMasterRace crap but this is an excellent Flow chart that summarizes how to spend your money.

I would also suggest the putting money in your wallet beforehand as well.

And finally don't have you payment details saved! it makes it too terrifyingly easy to add just a few dollars more.

You can do what I did and just give yourself 30 bucks per day to buy games with, with everything you buy having to fit within that sum and all unspent money carrying over to the next day. Even though I did it out of pure stinginess at first, it became a rather interesting exercise in resource management, as I had to put serious thought into what I spent my money on. If you're anything like me, you'll quickly end up puzzling your way out of seemingly insurmountable choices. If you combine that with the PC Master Race sale flowchart and only buy games during sales, then you can get quite a lot of game for your money. I suggest you try it.
